cards.name: Beat cell grading window
cards.summary: Presses and expected notes are collapsed to a cell index inside the beat, and only equal cell indices count as a hit
cards.behavior: Every press is recorded with the frame offset at which it landed. When the line closes, the grader shifts those offsets so the line starts inside a beat window, converts the result to tick units, and gives each press a cell index by counting how often the per-beat mask bit changed between the beat start and that tick. An expected note gets its index from the same walk, so the two agree only when they fall inside the same mask run. Three masks are provided: a normal curve, a late-shifted curve that forgives answers behind the beat, and a sparse curve with fewer valid cells. A press that arrives more than a quarter beat before the line opens is discarded before grading, so mashing ahead of the call never fills the press buffer. The scene reacts to the outcome indirectly: a graded line only chooses which script line runs next, and that line carries its own draw table, so a cell decision selects the next camera and model sequence instead of moving anything directly.

constants.name: normalCellMask
constants.unit: cell mask over 24 cells per beat, resampled every 4 ticks at 96 ticks per beat

constants.name: sparseCellMask
constants.unit: cell mask over 24 cells per beat, resampled every 4 ticks at 96 ticks per beat

constants.name: cellsPerBeat
constants.unit: cells per beat on the 96 tick musical clock, walked once per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: ticksPerCell
constants.unit: ticks per cell at 96 ticks per beat, converted once per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: beatTickWrap
constants.unit: ticks per beat, wrapped once per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: earlyPressGuard
constants.unit: ticks at 96 ticks per beat, tested on every press at 60 Hz

cards.name: Late answer second pass
cards.summary: The same line is compared twice, the second time with every expected note pushed two cells later, and the better tally wins
cards.behavior: A line is never graded by one comparison. The matcher first walks the captured presses against the expected notes on the normal grid, then shifts the expected notes two cells later on the same grid and walks again, and keeps whichever tally is larger. Shifting the expectations rather than the presses means a player who answers consistently behind the beat is measured against a grid that matches their timing, while a player who answers on time is unaffected because the second pass cannot beat the first. The late curve uses its own bit mask, so the tolerance is expressed as a cell geometry rather than as an added tolerance term, and the two passes share the same interpolation and counting code.

constants.name: lateCellMask
constants.unit: cell mask over 24 cells per beat, resampled every 4 ticks at 96 ticks per beat

constants.name: lateCellShift
constants.unit: cells at 4 ticks per cell, applied to every expected note once per judged line at 60 Hz

capabilities: late tolerance expressed as a cell curve

cards.name: Paired hit weighting
cards.summary: Matched note and press pairs count double minus the number of presses, so extra presses cost points immediately
cards.behavior: The tally walks every expected note against every captured press. In the full mode a pair counts only when both the cell index and the button agree; in the reduced mode only the cell index is compared and one button can carry an entire line. The result is twice the pair count minus the press count, so each extra press erodes the score while each correct pair adds two, and reward and penalty come out of one expression instead of two passes. A stricter variant of the same walk also subtracts the difference between the expected and captured press counts, which is what charges an answer that has the right shape but the wrong length. Captured presses live in a fixed per-line buffer that stops accepting entries once it is full, which bounds the matching work.

constants.name: pairWeight
constants.unit: points per matched pair, summed per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: pressBufferCap
constants.unit: presses stored per judged line at 60 Hz

capabilities: pair matching on cell and button
double weight versus extra press cost

cards.name: Sustained run minimum
cards.summary: A line that reads as a continuous run demands a press count derived from its own length
cards.behavior: For a run line the grader converts the line length in ticks into a required press count by dividing by twenty-four, rounding up, and adding three. Falling short of that count marks the run as broken. A broken run does not merely lose the points it would have earned: the assembled line total is replaced by a flat penalty, so a run answered with too few presses scores worse than the same line answered with stray presses. The extra three presses absorb the first and last taps of a run, where players typically enter late or leave early, and because the requirement grows with line length a long run demands proportionally more presses.

constants.name: runTickUnit
constants.unit: ticks per counted press at 96 ticks per beat, measured once per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: runPadding
constants.unit: extra presses per run line, applied once per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: brokenRunPenalty
constants.unit: points per broken run line, applied once per judged line at 60 Hz

capabilities: flat penalty replacing the line total

cards.name: Line score assembly
cards.summary: Twelve buckets weighted in sixteenths across three mask passes are summed into one line score
cards.behavior: Each grading routine stores its raw count in its own bucket, and every bucket is multiplied by that routine's weight and divided by sixteen, so the weight column behaves as sixteenths of a point per event. The line is graded three times, twice with the normal curve and once with the sparse curve, and each pass fills its own bucket set. At the top rank the coverage, meter count and sustain buckets are forced to zero so a near perfect line cannot be punished through them. The final total adds the twelve buckets, collapses to zero when the all-key coverage bucket fires, and is replaced by the run penalty when the sustained-run bucket fires.

constants.name: bucketWeightDivisor
constants.unit: divisor for bucket weights, applied per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: bucketCount
constants.unit: buckets summed per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: gradingPasses
constants.unit: mask passes per judged line at 60 Hz

cards.name: Rank ladder and stage result
cards.summary: One rank step per judged line across seventeen entries, and only the top two display bands clear the stage
cards.behavior: After each judged line the performer's rank level moves one notch up or down a seventeen entry ladder. The ladder folds into five display bands: a top band, a good band, a bad band, an awful band, and an end band used when the player has fallen as far as the game allows. A top band exam moves the rank against the pattern threshold; a good band exam moves it only when the line score clears the threshold or collapses to zero, and otherwise drifts toward good; bad and awful band exams move purely on whether the line score was positive. Reduced single button play and the easy table clamp a good band result at good, so those modes cannot drop a player into the bad band. The stage result reads the display band of the final rank: only the top and good bands record a clear of that stage, everything else returns the player to selection with no record.

constants.name: ladderEntries
constants.unit: ladder entries, stepped once per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: topBand
constants.unit: display band index, read once per stage result at 60 Hz

constants.name: goodBand
constants.unit: display band index, read once per stage result at 60 Hz

constants.name: thresholdDivisor
constants.unit: divisor on the pattern threshold, applied once per judged line at 60 Hz

cards.name: Answer loop until ten clean answers
cards.summary: A call and repeat segment repeats itself until ten answers are graded clean
cards.behavior: Some segments are taught in a call and repeat style: a short call is played, the player answers it, the answer is graded, and a counter advances only when the answer was clean. The counter is drawn as two marks per clean answer. The segment releases when the counter reaches ten; while it is short the game jumps back to the earlier line and replays the call, provided the line sequence holds a loop target to jump to. When no loop target exists the segment releases anyway, so a player who keeps failing is not stranded. The same threshold is reused where the bonus game reads the number of cleared lines, capped at ten before being compared with its own target count.

constants.name: cleanAnswersToPass
constants.unit: clean answers per segment, tested once per line at 60 Hz

constants.name: marksPerAnswer
constants.unit: meter marks per clean answer, drawn once per judged line at 60 Hz

constants.name: clearedLineCap
constants.unit: cleared lines counted at most, read once per bonus decision at 60 Hz

cards.name: Automatic pattern level ramp
cards.summary: The played pattern level is re-rolled from a weighted row after each chart segment
cards.behavior: When the player is not on a fixed level the game adjusts pattern difficulty itself. At the end of a chart segment it reduces the outcome table to a signed step, adds that step to the control level, and clamps the result into the range zero through fifteen. The next pattern level is then drawn by rolling a value below one hundred and walking that level's percentage row until the running sum passes the roll, so the row behaves as a weighted distribution instead of a fixed sequence. When the result differs from the previous level the performer's current line restarts from its beginning so the new pattern is read from the top. Recorded replay data replaces this whole step with the level stored in the recording, and a segment with a fixed level bypasses the roll entirely.

constants.name: levelRowEntries
constants.unit: entries per weight row, walked once per chart segment at 60 Hz

constants.name: rollRange
constants.unit: values in the level roll, drawn once per chart segment at 60 Hz

constants.name: lowestLevel
constants.unit: lowest pattern level, clamped once per chart segment at 60 Hz

constants.name: highestLevel
constants.unit: highest pattern level, clamped once per chart segment at 60 Hz

cards.name: Waiting a line while the scene cuts
cards.summary: A line can wait while a move walks to a later line, then resume on the musical clock
cards.behavior: A line can hand control to a short move: the current line is flagged as waiting, every other performer is paused outright, and a dedicated move walks from the current line to a target line at a target musical time. While waiting the performer skips its timing checks and its input grading, so presses during the cut are not charged against the line that is leaving. On waking, the destination line's own frame position is recomputed from the target time through its tempo, the note source is switched to the correct audio channel, and the time base is switched between the video clock and the disc audio clock depending on how the destination line declares its timing. Only then does the line resume, starting from the converted frame.

constants.name: waitStatus
constants.unit: status bit, tested every frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: waitEndStatus
constants.unit: status bit, tested every frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: pauseStatus
constants.unit: status bit, tested every frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: framesPerBeatMinute
constants.unit: frames times beats-per-minute divisor at 60 Hz vsync

constants.name: halfTickOffset
constants.unit: beat units at 96 units per beat, added per wake up at 60 Hz

cards.name: Song clock from frame or disc time
cards.summary: The musical clock is derived from either the video frame counter or the streamed audio position
cards.behavior: Two sources feed the same song clock. On the video path the frame counter is multiplied by ninety-six and by the stage tempo, offset by half a beat unit, and divided by the frames-per-minute constant, which turns a frame count into musical units at ninety-six per beat. On the audio path the streamed position is read back and divided by the same ratio to recover frames, with a half tick added before the division so the result rounds to the nearest unit instead of truncating. Both paths publish a sample count for the audio streamer, which keeps the music and the judge on the same position when a line changes tempo. The frame counter itself is a bank of fifty-one independent channels incremented once per vertical blank, so several lines can hold separate timing without sharing a counter, and a line can be handed a converted time when it wakes.

constants.name: ticksPerBeat
constants.unit: musical units per beat, one update per vsync frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: framesPerBeatMinute
constants.unit: frames times beats-per-minute divisor at 60 Hz vsync

constants.name: halfBeatOffset
constants.unit: half a beat unit in the same numerator scale at 60 Hz vsync

constants.name: roundingHalfTick
constants.unit: beat units at 96 per beat, added per audio clock read at 60 Hz

constants.name: clockChannels
constants.unit: channels incremented once per vsync callback at 60 Hz

cards.name: Camera cuts from the scene timeline
cards.summary: A camera entry takes the scene camera for the length of its own clip and cancels every other camera entry
cards.behavior: The scene timeline is a list of frame stamped entries. A camera entry hands the scene camera to one camera data block and runs for that block's frame length, and every other camera entry in the scene is disabled as soon as one becomes active, so exactly one camera drives the scene at any time. Position entries obey the same exclusivity: activating one cancels other position entries bound to the same model, which stops two tracks fighting over one model transform. An entry can also chain onto whatever is already running in its slot, in which case the new clip starts at the running clip's current frame plus one instead of at zero, and it can store its own time on the way out or restore that stored time on the way in, which is how a repeated shot keeps continuity across a cut. Entries that overrun their clip length are dropped from the active set instead of holding the slot.

constants.name: cameraEntryOpcode
constants.unit: timeline opcode, evaluated per timeline frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: storeTimeBit
constants.unit: entry status bit, evaluated per timeline frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: restoreTimeBit
constants.unit: entry status bit, evaluated per timeline frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: chainTimeBit
constants.unit: entry status bit, evaluated per timeline frame at 60 Hz

cards.name: Press held model animation
cards.summary: Some model clips wait at their last frame until the button that owns them is released
cards.behavior: An animation entry can be marked as waiting for input. Once such an entry is running, the timeline reads the press channel bound to it every frame: above a first held value the entry keeps advancing, and above a higher held value it advances twice as fast, which lets a held press run the model animation at double speed. When the press data disappears, or the channel reports no pressure at all, the timeline drives the entry's read head to the end of the clip and clears the animation job, so the model stops on its final pose instead of stalling mid clip. Clips are addressed in half frame steps, so a fractional frame position is resolved by averaging the neighbouring keyframe entries, and an entry whose wrap bit is set loops its read head modulo the clip span rather than ending.

constants.name: holdThreshold
constants.unit: press value steps, checked per timeline frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: fastHoldThreshold
constants.unit: press value steps, checked per timeline frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: halfFramePair
constants.unit: float frame entries per keyframe index, averaged per rendered frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: wrapBit
constants.unit: entry status bit, evaluated per timeline frame at 60 Hz

cards.name: Camera focal length and defocus
cards.summary: Focal length, defocus and depth level come from the selected camera's tracks or from the scene defaults
cards.behavior: A scene holds one selected camera plus a default camera. Once a camera is selected, focal length, defocus length and depth level are read from that camera's tracks at the scene's current camera time, but only when the camera header advertises the track set; otherwise the scene's own defaults are returned and the scene still renders with a sensible projection. A focal length at or below zero is replaced by the smallest positive float, which stops a malformed track from producing a division by zero deeper in the projection path. After the frame is submitted the renderer runs the defocus pass only when the focal length is non-zero, so a scene that does not want the effect pays nothing for it. The depth buffer format decides the precision reported to the effect, from sixteen bits up to thirty-two.

constants.name: cameraTrackFlag
constants.unit: camera header flag, read once per rendered frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: depthBufferBits
constants.unit: bits of depth precision, reported once per rendered frame at 60 Hz

capabilities: defocus pass gated on focal length

cards.name: Model draw order in the scene
cards.summary: Scene models are split into depth sorted, overlay, ordinary and screen layers before drawing
cards.behavior: Before a scene renders, its model list is rebuilt into a draw order. Models marked as screen space are detached into their own list that is drawn after everything else. Models carrying the depth order flag are inserted into a list sorted by their stored depth key, so their emission order is controlled by that key rather than by load order. Models carrying the overlay flag are collected separately and placed after the sorted group, and the remaining ordinary models follow. The renderer then sorts its collected transmit entries by a depth key before merging them into the display list, so the same geometry can resolve differently depending on how far the camera is from each part.

constants.name: depthOrderFlag
constants.unit: model header flag, evaluated once per drawn frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: overlayFlag
constants.unit: model header flag, evaluated once per drawn frame at 60 Hz

cards.name: Keyframe track sampling
cards.summary: Time is mapped to a segment by a cached search, then interpolated by spline, linear blend or held value
cards.behavior: Animation, camera and visibility data are stored as keyframe tracks. Sampling a track first locates the segment containing the requested time: the search reuses the segment found on the previous request and only falls back to a binary search when the request leaves that neighbourhood, which makes frame by frame sampling cheap. The track mode then selects the interpolator, either a spline that blends the keyed value with its incoming and outgoing tangents, a straight blend between two keys, or a held value with no blending. A track flagged as looping wraps the requested time into the track length before the search, so a repeating clip needs no duplicated keys. Node visibility is a track of its own: a node whose track evaluates false is skipped for that frame, and a node is hidden whenever its parent node is not visible.

constants.name: loopFlag
constants.unit: track flag, tested once per sampled frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: vectorsPerSegment
constants.unit: four component vectors per segment, sampled once per animation frame at 60 Hz

constants.name: parentVisibilityFlag
constants.unit: node flag, evaluated once per animation frame at 60 Hz

cards.name: Transformed model bounds
cards.summary: Local bounds are transformed by the model matrix and merged into a running world box
cards.behavior: Each model keeps a local bounding box and the scene keeps a running box. Updating the running box transforms the model's two local corners by the model matrix on the vector unit, once for the minimum corner and once for the maximum, and merges the results with a component wise minimum and maximum. The matrix is read as four sixteen byte rows, which is exactly what each corner transform consumes. Because the merge happens every frame, a model that a node animation moves or rotates contributes a box that grows to cover its animated travel rather than only its rest pose, and a second model merged into the same running box extends it instead of replacing it.

constants.name: matrixRowStride
constants.unit: bytes per row of the four by four matrix, consumed once per rendered frame at 60 Hz

capabilities: component wise min and max merge
